_readme: PROTOTYPE_001 -- the first serious breadboard prototype from the user's
hardware-scaling plan: two independent Field/Void magnetic memory state
machines (A and B, each a real TQ2-L-5V-class latching relay driven by
its own DRV8833-class H-bridge half), an M4-style router that issues
GPIO-level write commands but does NOT own the magnetic memory itself,
real physical contact readback (never assumed from the command that was
issued), and a fast/oversight/override timing chain built from real RC
delays feeding SN74HC14-class Schmitt-trigger gates. Run with:
node simulate.js experiments/prototype_001.json
Every part here is an ordinary, already-validated real component from
js/circuit.js (battery, resistor, capacitor, wire, diffsource,
hbridge, latchrelay, schmitt) -- the solver has no idea this board is
called PROTOTYPE_001 or that a node means 'SENSEA'; those are labels
declared in nodeNames/measurements purely for this file's own
readability and for the events/persistence/traces checks to refer to.
Circuit:
- bat1: one 5V rail pair (railTP/railBM) shared by everything, exactly
like a real breadboard power rail spanning the whole board.
- in1A/in2A/in1B/in2B: four diffsource parts standing in for M4's real
GPIO-class logic outputs (5V/0V, 100ohm source impedance -- a real
push-pull digital driver's output impedance, not an ideal voltage
source). M4 only ever touches these four lines -- it has no other
electrical connection to the magnetic memory, matching the
requirement that M4 route without owning the memory.
- hbA/hbB: one DRV8833-class H-bridge channel per relay coil, each
with real body-diode flyback, real propagation delay, real input
threshold, and real undervoltage lockout.
- lrA/lrB: the two real latching relays. Each coil is electrically a
single-winding memorycore (same square-loop Hc/remanence/switchTau
dynamics, the same code path, not a special case), and each has a
genuinely separate mechanical contact pair.
- Real contact-sense circuit (never assume the command = success):
each relay's COM contact is wired straight to the +5V rail, and its
NO contact is pulled down to GND through a 100k resistor. Closed
(Field/set) pulls the sense node to ~5V through the real ~0.05ohm
contact; open (Void/reset) leaves it pulled to ~0V by the 100k --
a real logic-level swing that genuinely depends on the mechanical
armature having actually moved, not on what was commanded.
- Fast/Oversight/Override timing chain (tapped off SENSEA as ONE
representative channel -- duplicating the same RC+Schmitt pattern
per channel, or building a true analog differential front end
before the taps, is the same pattern repeated and is deferred for
scope, noted honestly rather than faked):
Fast:      SENSEA -> sgFast directly (bounded only by the
Schmitt's own ~15ns propagation delay -- 'fast' here
really means 'no deliberate added delay', the actual
floor is the relay's own ms-scale switching time).
Oversight: FAST_OUT -> 10k/1uF RC (tau=10ms) -> sgOversight.
Override:  FAST_OUT -> 25k/1uF RC (tau=25ms) -> sgOverride, a
real, larger, separately visible delay before the
override tap agrees with the fast path.
Real problem found (and fixed) while building this, kept here as
an honest record rather than quietly corrected away: the first
version tapped both RC networks directly off the raw SENSEA node
(no buffer). Real capacitor charge from the 10k/25k RC legs then
fed back INTO the sense node itself, capacitively loading it and
slowing even the 'fast' path's own transition to ~100ms+ instead
of the relay's real few-ms mechanical time -- a genuine hardware
mistake a real bench build could make, not a solver bug (proven
by tracing the exact 10k/1uF and 25k/1uF time constants bleeding
back onto SENSEA). Fixed by tapping the oversight/override RC legs
off FAST_OUT (the Schmitt gate's own low-impedance push-pull
output) instead of the raw mechanical contact -- a real buffer,
exactly what a bench build needs here too.
IMPORTANT, disproving result found by actually running this (not
papered over): the 'Diff' measurement (SENSEA - SENSEB) that a
differential readout would naturally reach for CANNOT distinguish real
Void/Void (both relays open, Diff~0V) from real Field/Field conflict
(both relays closed, Diff~0V) -- a plain difference silently coerces
conflict into 'center'. Real conflict detection needs both sense lines
read independently (e.g. 'both high' vs 'both low' are different
physical states even though they subtract to the same number), which
is why this file's events list watches SENSEA and SENSEB separately
in addition to declaring the Diff measurement, and the conflict stages
at the end exist specifically to surface this rather than assume it.
Explicitly NOT implemented in this pass (deferred, not hidden):
- A true analog differential front end or per-channel oversight/
override taps for BOTH relays (only SENSEA's chain is built; SENSEB
is read directly as a named node for the conflict check above).
- Override actually reversing/cancelling a route in closed-loop
fashion -- this file only proves the override tap sees the real
delayed readback; using that to command a reversal is a follow-up.
- Contact bounce / coil-heating / temperature evolution over the
experiment's real timescale (the underlying components model these
already -- see LATCHRELAY_SPEC/HBRIDGE_SPEC in circuit.js -- this
experiment's dt/duration were not specifically tuned to surface them).
- The 100+ cycle repeated-run statistics harness (separate task).
Every write stage is followed by a real coast (no-drive) hold stage --
the magnetic state during the hold is held by real remanence alone,
not by sustained drive current, which is the actual persistence claim
being tested (see the 'persistence' block below).
